findings.title: Queries are now template-interpolated more than once
findings.body:
`runSplitQuery` now calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables` on every target, but the same request still goes through `datasource.runQuery`, which normally applies template variables again before sending to the backend. On the sharding path it is worse: `runShardSplitQuery` interpolates first, then `runSplitQuery` interpolates every sub-request again. The updated test confirms this, expecting 5 calls for 4 requests.

Loki's `applyTemplateVariables` is not idempotent. It appends ad-hoc filters (`request.filters`), so each pass can add those matchers again. It also re-runs variable replacement on already-interpolated text, so a variable value that contains `$something` or regex-escaped characters is substituted or escaped a second time. The result is duplicated filters, wrong expressions, and wasted work.

Interpolation should happen exactly once: either skip it in `runSplitQuery` when called from the shard path, or remove it from the downstream `runQuery` path.

findings.title: $__range detection now runs on already-interpolated expressions
findings.body: `querySupportsSplitting` uses `isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr)` to keep queries containing `$__range` out of time splitting. Because interpolation now happens on line 299, before the partition, `$__range` (and `$__auto` resolved to a range) has already been replaced by a concrete duration. The check therefore no longer matches, and these queries are silently split into per-day chunks. That is exactly the case the guard and its comment were written to prevent. The range-variable check should run on the raw expression before interpolation.

findings.title: Interpolated targets are re-interpolated inside runSplitQuery
findings.body: `runShardSplitQuery` interpolates the targets, injects shard selectors, and then passes each sub-request to `runSplitQuery`. `runSplitQuery` calls `applyTemplateVariables` again on those already-interpolated, shard-modified expressions, using the same `scopedVars` and `filters`. This double pass is redundant and risks re-applying ad-hoc filters. It also lets the second pass alter the injected `__stream_shard__` matchers or user values that contain `$`. Interpolation should be done in only one of the two places, for example via a flag or by keeping it in the shared entry point.
